collection.description: The cousin's own village, far to the south, has had three bad harvests, and the family is hungry.

ask.text:
A trader brings a message for (name): (his/her) cousin, who left the island as a child with (his/her) parents, wants to come home. The cousin's own village, far to the south, has had three bad harvests, and the family is hungry. The message asks only whether there is room.
(Name) hasn't seen this cousin since they were both small enough to share a sleeping mat. The village's stores are not overflowing. Should (name) send word to come, or go and fetch them personally, in case the journey is too hard?

c1o1.text: A month later a canoe comes in from the south, and (name)'s cousin wades ashore with a partner and a baby, thin and sunburnt and holding the carved shell. The two cousins recognise each other at once, somehow, after all those years. {#made:The village has room for only one of them|The village shares out the stores to feed three more, and nobody minds}.

c1o2.text: The canoe that comes brings the cousin and two children: a long-legged teenager who has paddled half the way, and a small child who has been seasick the whole time. The cousin's partner, (he/she) explains quietly, didn't survive the last bad harvest. (Name) takes {#made:in one of them, as the village has no room for more|in two of them, as the village has no room for more|them all in}, and the teenager, who has never seen so much fish in (his/her) life, eats until (he/she) has to lie down.

c1.text: (Name) sends back a carved shell with the trader: a fish, which in the old way means "come home." Then (he/she) waits, watching the south every morning...

c2o1.text: (Name) finds (his/her) cousin's village in a bad way, and brings {#made:the cousin home, as the village has no room for more|the cousin, the cousin's partner and their baby home}. On the long journey back, (name) does most of the steering, reading the stars, the swells and the birds, and by the time they land, (he/she) is a far better sailor than when (he/she) left.

c2o2.text: At the cousin's village, (name) learns that the family left a week ago, for another island, where they had heard there was work. Nobody knows which. (Name) leaves the carved shell with the village elder, in case they come back. Nine days home, empty-handed. (Name) watches the south every morning for a year.

c2.text: (Name) loads a canoe with dried fish, water and two strong paddlers, and sets out south. The journey takes nine days...
